title: Esther 4
paragraphs: ¹ When Mordecai learned of everything that had happened, he tore his clothes and put on sackcloth and ashes. He went through the city, crying out loudly and bitterly. ² He came as far as the king's gate, but could go no further, since no one was allowed to enter the king's gate wearing sackcloth. ³ In every province, wherever the king's command and decree reached, there was great mourning among the Jews — fasting, weeping, and wailing — and many lay in sackcloth and ashes. ⁴ When Esther's maids and eunuchs told her what was happening, she was deeply distressed. She sent clothes for Mordecai to put on so he could take off his sackcloth, but he refused them. ⁵ Then Esther summoned Hatach, one of the king's eunuchs assigned to attend her, and instructed him to go to Mordecai and find out what was wrong and why.

⁶ So Hatach went out to Mordecai in the city square in front of the king's gate. ⁷ Mordecai told him everything that had happened to him, including the exact amount of money Haman had promised to pay into the royal treasury to buy the destruction of the Jews. ⁸ He also gave him a copy of the written decree that had been issued in Shushan authorizing their annihilation, so that Hatach could show it to Esther and explain it to her. Mordecai charged him to urge Esther to go into the king's presence to plead for mercy and intercede for her people. ⁹ Hatach returned and told Esther exactly what Mordecai had said. ¹⁰ Then Esther spoke to Hatach again and gave him a message for Mordecai:

¹¹ "All the king's servants and the people of his provinces know that there is a single law for anyone — man or woman — who comes to the king in the inner court without being summoned: they are put to death. The only exception is if the king extends his golden scepter, which means they may live. And I have not been summoned to come to the king for thirty days." ¹² When Mordecai was told what Esther had said, ¹³ he sent back this reply: "Don't think for a moment that you will escape in the palace any more than all the other Jews. ¹⁴ If you stay silent at a time like this, relief and deliverance for the Jews will come from somewhere else — but you and your father's family will be destroyed. And who knows? Perhaps you have been brought to your royal position for such a time as this." ¹⁵ Then Esther sent this answer back to Mordecai:

¹⁶ "Go and gather all the Jews in Shushan and fast for me. Do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. My maids and I will fast as well. After that, I will go to the king, even though it is against the law — and if I die, I die." ¹⁷ So Mordecai went and did everything Esther had instructed him to do.
